A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReGNet and its multi-task extension. All pages, including appendices, are readable, and the methods, equations, tables, and figures can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original ReGNet and ReGNet-MT prediction errors, reciprocal-component and depth ablations, expert-selection analyses, and training-time measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds MatBench evaluations, linear-scalarization comparisons, and five-block depth results.

M1.justification: The local GNN, reciprocal Fourier-filter updates, pooling, and MoE decoder are retained. Section 3.4 newly specifies that local and global embedding updates are summed, clarifying the existing integration without establishing an algorithm change. The MoE formulation moves to Appendix C.

E1.justification: V2 adds MatBench formation-energy evaluation on e_form and exfoliation-energy prediction for 2D materials on jdft2d (Section 5 and Appendix B.1). This expands the evaluated material corpus and introduces a distinct property/domain task. All original Materials Project and JARVIS tasks remain.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated MODNet, coGN, and M3GNet comparisons on MatBench (Table 3). Tables 12–13 also introduce ReGNet-LS, using linear scalarization, as a direct multi-task comparator on JARVIS and Materials Project. The original single-task baseline sets are retained.

E3.justification: Reported JARVIS depths change from three to four blocks for OPT bandgap and four to five for Ehull (v1 Table 6; v2 Table 7). Added experiments introduce MatBench MAE/RMSE evaluation and three-versus-five-task LS settings. Existing Materials Project/JARVIS splits and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 extends depth sensitivity from three/four blocks to five, showing an Ehull benefit but slight deterioration elsewhere (Table 11), and adds three-versus-five-task LS comparisons (Table 12). The reciprocal-removal ablation and expert-selection analysis are retained; relocating the full ablation into the main text is not new analysis.

E5.justification: V1 provides no repeated-run uncertainty reporting. V2 reports MatBench means and standard deviations over five runs (Section 5.1 and Table 3). This reporting is confined to the added benchmark and does not establish additional runs for retained results.

E6.justification: V2 adds MatBench, LS, and five-block results. ReGNet's MatBench MAEs are 16.1 ± 0.2 and 31.6 ± 6.3 meV/atom. JARVIS Table 2 changes OPT bandgap from 0.127 to 0.126 eV and Ehull from 48 to 43 meV alongside changed depths. The four-block ablation's OPT value also changes from 0.127 to 0.126. Original Materials Project, ReGNet-MT, and timing values are retained.

T1.justification: The crystal definitions, Fourier equations, reciprocal-lattice mathematics, GNN equations, and MoE formulation are unchanged. The reciprocal relationship added to Section 2.2 already appeared in Appendix A.1. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: V2 recasts multi-property prediction from a headline contribution with explicit best-bandgap claims into an exploratory extension. Its contribution list newly claims the first end-to-end crystal message-passing framework with trainable Fourier-space filters, while the abstract and conclusion emphasize ReGNet performance across three benchmarks.

C2.justification: Appendix B.5 newly interprets five-block behavior through thermodynamic-stability sensitivity and possible overfitting or optimization difficulties. Appendix C.5 explains multi-task degradation through gradient conflict and increasing task count. Section 6 also qualifies the multi-task extension as an initial attempt.

D1.justification: V2 documents MatBench depths, learning rates, epochs, and neighbor counts in Table 10, revises JARVIS depth entries, and clarifies embedding integration in Section 3.4. Existing embedding specifications, GPU information, and the promise to release code upon acceptance remain.

R1.justification: The introduction and new reciprocal-space discussion in Section 4 substantially sharpen novelty positioning: v2 distinguishes bulk-crystal modeling from EwaldMP's molecular/surface setting and contrasts learnable filters with Crystalformer's fixed reciprocal features. References for MatBench, MODNet, M3GNet, and coGN are added; Bloch's 1929 citation is removed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, and experimental narrative are substantially revised. Multi-task motivation, background, related work, decoder discussion, and interpretation are consolidated into Appendix C. Experimental subsections are reordered, and results are organized by benchmark.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 become smaller figures with surrounding text. Multi-task rows and the expert heatmap move into Appendix C, while the full reciprocal ablation moves into the main text with redesigned columns. MatBench result/settings tables and separate depth and LS comparison tables are added. The efficiency table gains a model-type column.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical support through the added exfoliation-energy task with five-run uncertainty, direct LS comparisons absent in v1, and clearer evidence of depth-related tradeoffs. Consolidating multi-task material also improves focus. These are useful incremental gains, although uncertainty reporting remains confined to MatBench and implementation details for the new LS comparisons remain sparse.
